diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\phi$ denotes the rational cubic trigonometric FIF. \cite{chand2015positivity}.

issues.failure_explanation: The first step of the error estimate asserts \|\phi_\epsilon-\phi\|_\infty = \|\lambda_j(\phi_\epsilon-\phi) + M_{j,\epsilon} - M_j\|_\infty by substituting the functional equation on each I_j under a single horizontal map. But \phi_\epsilon satisfies its recursion under L_{j,\epsilon} (orientation-reversing when \epsilon_j=1), while the classical RCTFIF \phi satisfies \phi(L_{j,0}(t)) = \lambda_j\phi(t) + M_j(t) under the orientation-preserving map. Since L_{j,\epsilon} \neq L_{j,0} on reversed segments, \phi(L_{j,\epsilon}(t)) is not \lambda_j\phi(t)+M_j(t), so the pointwise identity behind the norm equality is false there and the derived bound \|\phi_\epsilon-\phi\|_\infty \le \|M_{j,\epsilon}-M_j\|_\infty/(1-|\lambda|_\infty) is unjustified. The identity is valid only when all \epsilon_j=0, in which case \phi_\epsilon=\phi and the whole estimate is vacuous.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the pointwise identity by an operator comparison, \|\phi_\epsilon-\phi\|_\infty \le \|T_\epsilon\phi - T_0\phi\|_\infty/(1-|\lambda|_\infty), and estimate the misaligned terms \phi(L_{j,\epsilon}^{-1}s)-\phi(L_{j,0}^{-1}s) and M_j(L_{j,\epsilon}^{-1}s)-M_j(L_{j,0}^{-1}s) via moduli of continuity of \phi and M_j, restating the bound with these additional terms.
issues.overall_effect: The bound for \|\phi_\epsilon-\phi\|_\infty, and hence the first term of Theorem 4.2's estimate, is unsupported exactly in the zipper case (any \epsilon_j=1) that the paper advertises. No other labelled result depends on it.
issues.title: Zipper-versus-classical error identity ignores the reversed horizontal maps
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained replacement of the comparison argument using standard fixed-point and modulus-of-continuity tools; the theorem survives as an error bound of the same type with extra terms and there are no dependent results, but the core recursion must be re-derived and the stated bound changes, so it exceeds a local routine fix.

issues.failure_explanation: Several steps are invalid. (i) \xi is defined as a maximum of |q_j(\theta)|, but bounding |c/q| by |c|/\xi requires a lower bound on |q| (a positive minimum); with \xi a maximum the inequality goes the wrong way. (ii) After the triangle inequality one norm term enters the asserted upper bound with a minus sign, which cannot occur in an upper bound. (iii) For \epsilon_j=1, d_{j+\epsilon_j}-d_j = d_{j+1}-d_j while d_{j+1-\epsilon_j}-d_{j+1} = -(d_{j+1}-d_j), so the derivative terms combine as \alpha B_1 + \delta B_2, not \alpha B_1 - \delta B_2 as written (the written bracket can even be negative). (iv) The final step uses \|f_{j+\epsilon_j}-f_j\|_\infty \le \Phi, which holds only for positive data, whereas Theorem 4.2 is stated for arbitrary data (only 2\Phi is available); with \gamma,\delta\to0, \alpha=\beta, f_{j+1}-f_j=2\Phi and zero derivatives the displayed intermediate bound \|M^\epsilon-M\| \le \|\epsilon\|(C\Phi + 4h_j\eta/\pi) is violated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the estimate: keep absolute values through the triangle inequality (no negative terms), use |q_{j,\epsilon}| \ge \min_{j,\theta}|q| > 0 (or the ratio bounds (\alpha B_0+\beta B_1)/q \le 1 etc. valid for non-negative parameters), correct the derivative-term sign to \alpha B_1 + \delta B_2, and use |f_{j+1}-f_j| \le 2\Phi (or restrict to positive data), restating Theorem 4.2 with the corrected constants.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit constants in Theorem 4.2's bound are unreliable and the intermediate bound is false within the theorem's stated generality, so Theorem 4.2 as stated is unproved and can fail for non-positive data. No downstream labelled results are affected.
issues.title: Estimate chain for \|M_{j,\epsilon}-M_j\| uses invalid inequalities; stated constants unjustified
issues.why_classification: Fixing this requires a full replacement of the estimate chain and changes the stated constants (the stated bound is false as written in its regime), which is more than a local routine repair; but it is contained in one proof, needs no new global architecture or advertised-scope loss, and a recognizably comparable bound survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $q_{j,\epsilon}(t) \neq 0, \forall t\in[t_1, t_n]$ and $|\lambda_j| < a_j, j\in \mathbb{N}_{n-1}$ is the vertical scaling factor.

issues.failure_explanation: The affine map fixed by L_{j,\epsilon}(t_1)=t_{j+\epsilon_j}, L_{j,\epsilon}(t_n)=t_{j+1-\epsilon_j} has slope a_j = (t_{j+1-\epsilon_j}-t_{j+\epsilon_j})/(t_n-t_1), which is negative whenever \epsilon_j=1 (orientation reversed). Hence condition (1) of Theorem 5.1, 0 \le \lambda_j < \min\{a_i,\dots\} (and likewise the construction's |\lambda_j|<a_j and the invoked C^1 condition |\lambda_j|<a_j), has no solution on any reversed segment: the theorem's hypothesis is unsatisfiable for precisely the reversed signatures, including \epsilon=(1,1,1,1,1,1) used in all the positivity figures. The Section 6 bounds are computed with |a_j| (e.g. 0.1333 = 2/15 = h_1/(t_n-t_1)), confirming the intended condition \lambda_j<|a_j|, but as written the theorem does not sanction the showcased parameters.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace a_i by |a_j| in condition (1) and |\lambda_j|<a_j by |\lambda_j|<|a_j| in the construction and in the invoked smoothness condition; the numerics already conform to this.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 5.1 is vacuous for every signature containing a reversed segment, so the paper's central positivity application (all figures use \epsilon=(1,1,1,1,1,1)) is unsupported as written; the numerical bounds silently use the corrected |a_j| version.
issues.title: Scaling-factor condition uses signed a_j, unsatisfiable on reversed segments
issues.why_classification: The least repair is a standard one-symbol correction (modulus on a_j), already implicitly used in the paper's own numerical bounds; the method, the theorem's conclusion, its proof structure, and all showcased applications survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Thus, ensuring the above inequalities guarantees that $p_{j,\epsilon}(\theta) > 0$, and hence, by Equation~\eqref{pos_con}, the interpolant $\phi_\epsilon$ remains strictly positive on $[t_1, t_n]$.

issues.failure_explanation: To conclude \phi_\epsilon(L_j(t)) = \lambda_j\phi_\epsilon(t) + M_{j,\epsilon}(t) > 0, the proof assumes \phi_\epsilon(t) \ge 0 on the whole interval — the non-strict form of exactly what is to be proved — and never establishes it. Non-negativity of the fixed point does not follow from p_{j,\epsilon}>0 alone; a necessary step is missing: the zipper Read–Bajraktarevi\'c operator maps the closed cone of non-negative continuous functions (with the prescribed endpoint values) into itself because \lambda_j\ge0 and M_{j,\epsilon}>0, so the unique fixed point (the uniform limit of non-negative iterates) is non-negative, and then \phi_\epsilon(L_j(t)) \ge M_{j,\epsilon}(t) > 0 yields strict positivity.

failure_location.quote: Assuming $\phi_\epsilon(t) \geq 0$ for all $t \in [t_1, t_n]$ and $0 \leq \lambda_j < 1$, it suffices to ensure that the rational term $\frac{p_{j,\epsilon}(\theta)}{q_{j,\epsilon}(\theta)}$ is strictly non-negative over the interval.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the standard invariance argument: the zipper Read–Bajraktarevi\'c operator preserves the cone of non-negative functions in C(I) (\lambda_j\ge0, M_{j,\epsilon}>0), hence the fixed point is non-negative; strict positivity then follows from \phi_\epsilon(L_j(t)) \ge M_{j,\epsilon}(t) > 0.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem 5.1 is incomplete as written; the statement itself remains true under the stated conditions, so the effect is confined to the missing justification of non-negativity of the fixed point.
issues.title: Positivity proof assumes the conclusion \phi_\epsilon \ge 0
issues.why_classification: The gap is filled by a routine, standard few-line fixed-point/cone-invariance argument using tools already in the paper; the statement, conditions, and all applications survive, so the repair is short, local, and loses no content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Rigorous error analysis is presented to establish the convergence of the proposed zipper fractal interpolants to the underlying classical fractal functions, and subsequently, to the data-generating function.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and conclusion assert that the error analysis establishes/confirms convergence of the RCTZFIF to the data-generating function. Theorem 4.2 supplies only a fixed-mesh upper bound whose right-hand side does not tend to zero as h\to0: the first term tends to \|\epsilon\|_\infty C\Phi/(1-|\lambda|_\infty), a positive constant for every nontrivial signature (\|\epsilon\|_\infty=1 whenever any \epsilon_j=1), and the classical term \frac{|\lambda|_\infty}{1-|\lambda|_\infty}(E(h)+E^*(h)) is also non-vanishing for fixed \lambda. No regime (e.g. |\lambda|_\infty\to0 as the mesh refines) is stated under which the bound tends to zero, so the formal content does not imply convergence; the prose overstates what the paper establishes.

failure_location.quote: Theoretical analysis confirmed the convergence of the RCTZFIF to to the original data-generating function.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either sharpen the analysis into a genuine convergence proof — using |f_{j+1}-f_j|=O(h) and |d_{j+1}-d_j|=O(h) for C^3 data together with a stated scaling regime such as |\lambda|_\infty=O(h^3) (or o(1)) so that the right-hand side tends to zero — or weaken the abstract/conclusion to claim only a fixed-mesh error bound.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised convergence of the RCTZFIF to the data-generating function (abstract, convergence-section framing, and conclusion) is not delivered; only a fixed-mesh error estimate is established, and for nontrivial signatures the proved bound does not even tend to zero under mesh refinement.
issues.title: Convergence to the data-generating function claimed but not established by the proved bound
issues.why_classification: The least source-supported resolution is either a contained but nontrivial sharpening of the error analysis (a new estimate plus an explicitly stated scaling regime) or a limited weakening of the advertised claim; the interpolation construction and positivity results are unaffected, so there is no major loss, but the fix exceeds a local routine edit.
